title: Make a second scene and switch to it
summary: Add a scene, give it a source, and switch between scenes.

steps.say: Make sure the preview is one single picture, not split in two. Say done when it is.
hints: If you see two pictures side by side, Studio Mode is on.
Click Studio Mode in the Controls panel to turn it off.
steps.why: In normal mode, clicking a scene switches the output straight away.

steps.say: Click the plus button at the bottom left of the Scenes panel.

checks.prompt: Is a small window open asking for a scene name?

hints: Scenes is the panel at the far left of the bottom row.
You can also right-click empty space in the Scenes panel and choose Add.
steps.why: Each scene is a separate layout you can jump to.

steps.say: Type Be right back as the name, then press Enter.

checks.prompt: Does the Scenes panel list a scene called Be right back?

hints: Any name works; pick one that tells you what the scene is for.
Click OK if pressing Enter does nothing.
steps.why: Clear scene names make switching quick during a recording or stream.

steps.say: Click Be right back in the Scenes panel. The preview goes empty because the scene has no sources yet.

checks.prompt: Is the scene called Be right back highlighted, with an empty or black preview?

hints: New scenes start empty; that is expected.
Use the arrow keys in the Scenes list to move the highlight.
steps.why: An empty scene shows that sources belong to one scene, not to OBS as a whole.

steps.say: Now click your first scene, usually called Scene, to switch back.

checks.prompt: Does the preview show the screen capture again, with the first scene highlighted?

hints: It is the scene above Be right back in the list.
If you renamed it, pick the scene that holds your Display Capture.
steps.why: Switching scenes is how you change what viewers see without stopping.
